title: Protocol #02: Friction Fire Ignition (Primitive Bow Drill Method)
summary: Hypothermia in the wilderness can be fatal within 3 hours. Utilize high-speed rotational friction from a primitive bow drill combining dried oak heartwood and wild kudzu cordage to harvest live embers.

materials.name: Dry Oak Fire Board (HEARTH BOARD)
materials.desc: Bone-dry 2cm thick softwood or hardwood plank. Carve 45° V-notch to collect high-temperature carbon dust.

materials.name: Straight Willow Spindle (SPINDLE)
materials.desc: 2cm diameter, 20cm length straight and dense dry branch. Whittle both tips into conic pivots.

materials.name: Curved Ash Bow & Kudzu Cordage (BOW & STRING)
materials.desc: Resilient 60cm curved branch strung with twisted and dried wild kudzu fiber cord.

steps.title: Hearth V-Notch Carving & Spindle Mounting
steps.description: Carve a 45-degree V-notch into the hearth board rim. Wrap spindle once in bow string, hold vertically, and apply downward force using handhold socket.
steps.actionNote: > Action: Place a dry leaf or bark tray under the notch to prevent hot carbon dust from absorbing soil moisture.

steps.title: Reciprocal Sawing & Max Friction Heating
steps.description: Stroke the bow horizontally with long, rhythmic motions. Gradually accelerate speed under maximum torque until dense black smoke pours out.
steps.actionNote: > Science: High-speed rotational friction exceeds 400°C contact temp, igniting carbonized wood powder into a coherent glowing ember.

steps.title: Tinder Nest Transfer & Gentle Oxygen Ignition
steps.description: Gently transfer the glowing ember mass into a dry grass/leaf tinder nest. Blow long, steady exhalations until it bursts into open flame.
steps.actionNote: > Caution: Blowing violently will scatter and cool the fragile ember. Expand warmth gradually with deep, rhythmic breaths.

fatalMistake.title: Fatal Mistake: Halting bow motion prematurely upon initial smoke sighting.
fatalMistake.description: Smoke indicates heating, not a consolidated ember. Stopping before a dense glowing coal forms will cause immediate heat dissipation. Continue drilling at maximum output for 10 seconds after thick smoke emerges until a glowing coal is visible.
fatalMistake.consequence: Outcome: Physical exhaustion, palm blistering, and night hypothermia.
